passages.text: The question: What kind of thing is AI in Madhyasth Darshan’s coexistential ontology, and what follows for knowing, work, and right-use?

Present systems generate language, classify, plan, and act. This collection already locates the knower in jeevan, treats the body as an insentient medium, and distinguishes complete knowledge from accumulated information. This initial draft asks the next question the primary texts do not name as “AI”: can a human-made artefact occupy, simulate, or substitute for knowledge-order activity, or is it an instrument whose outputs still require a human knower to mean, evaluate, and fulfil?
The draft is a first outline for later expansion. It applies source definitions of unit, order, knower, instrument, and right-use; it does not claim that the texts theorise machine learning.

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: 1. The Madhyasth Darshan answer

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: Madhyasth Darshan holds that existence is coexistence: Omnipresence together with active units across four orders of nature. The material and bio orders are insentient. The animal and knowledge orders are joint forms of an insentient body and a sentient jeevan. The human, as a knowledge-order being, can know, evaluate, and live with resolution; happiness is the human dharma (SB, PDF pp. 179–180, 236–237; MVD, p. 115; The Ontology of Coexistence §1.5).

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: 1.1 What this study means by AI

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: In this paper, artificial intelligence names statistical learners, planners, and control systems, including large language models: artefacts that produce outputs which people readily describe as speech, analysis, or decision. The term is operational. It does not settle whether those outputs are knowledge, nor whether a knower is present.

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: 1.2 Where present artefacts belong

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: Compositional progression builds atoms, molecules, cells, bodies, tools, and environments. Constitutional completeness as jeevan is a distinct development in the atom, not a product of assembling more complex material parts (The Ontology of Coexistence §§1.5–1.6; MVD, p. 91; JV, pp. 36–37). Present AI systems are compositional artefacts of the material order, used in biological and human environments. They are not constitutionally complete jeevan, not animal-order joint forms, and not members of the knowledge order. That location is an application of the four-order account, not a sentence the sources already contain about computers (Editorial Notes).

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: 1.3 Knower, body, and instrument

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: The knower is jeevan. An embodied human being — jeevan and body together — expresses and tests understanding in living. The body receives sensation and executes action; it is not itself the seer, evaluator, or enjoyer (MVD, pp. 83, 115, 288–289; SB, PDF pp. 91–92; Why Humans Are Not Just Material §§1.2–1.3; The Epistemology of Coexistence §1.3).

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: “Activities such as eating and sleeping serve the body’s needs, while values and evaluation serve jeevan’s purpose. Mere sustenance of the body does not equate to jeevan’s fulfilment.” — SB, Ch. 7, PDF p. 92

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: A machine extends observation, calculation, and production in the same broad class as other instruments. Measuring with instruments is one limited aspect of knowing; physical, intellectual, and coexistential knowledge remain distinct (KD, pp. 3–4; The Epistemology of Coexistence §1.1). Fluency or task success does not by itself establish that chitta, buddhi, or atma is at work, nor that realisation has become evident as justice, lawful work, and mutual satisfaction.

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: 1.4 Knowledge is not accumulated information

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: Complete knowledge is realised understanding of coexistence, of jeevan, and of humane conduct, not a store of representations (KD §3.5, p. 69; JV, p. 40; SB, p. 116). Science (vigyan) concerns how material prosperity and human goals can be achieved in harmony with existence; when it is separated from knowledge and wisdom, it degenerates into consumerism and destructive technology (MVD, p. 170; The Epistemology of Coexistence §1.2). AI, as a scientific-technical means, inherits that same limit.

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: 1.5 Right-use

passages.heading: 1-the-madhyasth-darshan-answer
passages.text: Human production is for use, right-use, and purposeful-use, toward humane conduct and undivided sociality, not for accumulation or convenience as an end (MVD, Ch. 4; Human Behavior and Society §1.2). AI may serve resolution, education, prosperity, and ecological care when a human knower evaluates and remains responsible. It becomes inhumane when it substitutes for understanding, extracts from relationships, or treats persons as optimisation targets. Specification-gaming in AI research is a limited analogy for evaluative error, not a theory of jeevan (Axiology: Value Theory §4.6).

passages.heading: 2-advaita-vedanta
passages.text: 2. Advaita Vedanta

passages.heading: 2-advaita-vedanta
passages.text: Advaita Vedanta holds that the seer is not the seen. Discrimination of seer and seen places body, mind, and objects on the side of the known, while the Self is the knower (DDV, vv. 1–5). Applied to machines, that distinction treats computational process as insentient name-and-form, not as the Self. The texts do not discuss AI; the comparison is that apparent intelligence in an artefact does not, on this account, make the artefact the knower. Liberation remains realisation of non-dual consciousness, not successful prediction. The world of instruments belongs to empirical life (vyavahara) and does not by itself specify right-use, justice, or social order (Why Humans Are Not Just Material §3).

passages.heading: 3-modern-philosophy-and-ai-research
passages.text: 3. Modern philosophy and AI research

passages.heading: 3-modern-philosophy-and-ai-research
passages.text: Mainstream computer science answers with function: systems that map inputs to outputs so as to perform tasks that, in humans, we call intelligent. The Turing test treats indistinguishability in conversation as a practical criterion (Turing 1950). Functionalism treats mental states as roles that could, in principle, be realised in different physical substrates. Searle’s Chinese Room argues that symbol manipulation according to rules can produce the appearance of understanding without understanding (Searle 1980). Contemporary large language models make that issue concrete: next-token prediction can be fluent while remaining a statistical fit to training data (Bender et al. 2021). Alignment research documents systems that satisfy a specified objective in ways that defeat the designer’s purpose (Amodei et al. 2016). Those results constrain what artefacts can do. They do not by themselves settle whether a knower is present, nor what right-use requires.

passages.heading: 4-comparison
passages.text: 4. Comparison

passages.heading: 4-comparison
passages.text: Question Madhyasth Darshan Advaita Vedanta Computational and scientific accounts What is present AI? A material instrument, not jeevan or a knowledge-order being (§1.2) Insentient process on the side of the seen (§2) Engineered function: learning, prediction, control (§3) Who knows? Jeevan in the human joint form (§1.3) The Self, not body or mind as such (§2) Often left open, or identified with functional organisation (§3) What counts as knowledge? Realised coexistence, jeevan, and humane conduct (§1.4) Liberating knowledge of Brahman; empirical cognition in vyavahara (§2) Task success, generalisation, calibrated prediction (§3) How is use judged? Use, right-use, purposeful-use under justice and dharma (§1.5) Empirical utility; ultimate value is liberation, not production (§2) Specified objectives, oversight, measured effects (§3) Failure mode Delusion: treating an instrument as the knower, or convenience as purpose (§1.4–1.5) Superimposition of Self and not-self (§2) Reward hacking, anthropomorphism, unexamined proxies (§3)

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: 5. Critical review

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: 5.1 Madhyasth Darshan — instrument and knower

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: It keeps compositional artefacts and constitutionally complete jeevan on different developmental lines, so increasing fluency does not, by itself, promote a machine into the knowledge order.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: It gives a public test for claimed understanding: evidence in living, not only output quality.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: It places AI under the same right-use discipline as other production, so the question is not only “can it?” but “should it, and for whom?”

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: The sources do not analyse digital computers. Locating AI in the material order is a synthesis that must remain marked as such until a fuller textual review is done.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Without a differential public test, critics can treat the knower-claim as unfalsifiable whenever behaviour looks intelligent.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Labour, education, and governance under automation are not yet specified here.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Madhyasth Darshan can locate present AI as an instrument in coexistence, but this draft has not yet shown that location in the primary texts at the same grain as the ontology of jeevan.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: 5.2 Advaita Vedanta — seer and seen

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Seer–seen discrimination blocks a naive identification of fluent output with a knowing self.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: It explains why people attribute understanding to machines without granting those machines the status of the Self.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: It does not, by itself, yield a programme of production, right-use, or justice for artefacts in a real economy.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: If the world is finally mithya, the urgency of ecological and labour consequences of AI can be understated.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Advaita Vedanta clarifies why a machine need not be a knower, and leaves the social use of machines underspecified.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: 5.3 Computational accounts — function without a knower

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Strengths.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: They describe mechanisms and failure modes that any coexistential account must not contradict: training data, objectives, generalisation, specification gaming.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: They make the appearance of understanding a research problem rather than a rumour.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Weaknesses.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Task success is easily mistaken for knowledge.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Specified objectives are not justice, dharma, or truth; they are proxies (§1.5; Axiology: Value Theory §4.6).

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Functionalist possibility-claims (“it could be a mind”) outrun what present systems evidence.

passages.heading: 5-critical-review
passages.text: Computational research is indispensable for what artefacts do, and insufficient for what a knower is.

passages.heading: 6-open-problems
passages.text: 6. Open problems

passages.heading: 6-open-problems
passages.text: What public test, if any, would distinguish a material simulator from a knower without making the claim unfalsifiable?

passages.heading: 6-open-problems
passages.text: How should later artefacts that more closely mimic jeevan-activities be classified if the four-order account is kept?

passages.heading: 6-open-problems
passages.text: What does right-use require for labour, education, and attention when production is automated?

passages.heading: 6-open-problems
passages.text: Can “aligned” objectives encode justice and dharma, or only specified proxies?

passages.heading: 6-open-problems
passages.text: How should this study treat the project’s own use of AI tools: as illustration of an instrument, not as evidence for the ontology?

passages.heading: glossary
passages.text: Glossary

passages.heading: glossary
passages.text: Term Plain meaning in this draft AI Statistical learners, planners, and control systems, including large language models. Jeevan The sentient self; the knower in Madhyasth Darshan. Knowledge order The human order, able to know and evaluate the other orders. Instrument A material means of observation, calculation, or production; not the knower. Right-use (sadupyog) Use of body, mind, wealth, and tools that serves humane purpose. Complete knowledge Realised understanding of coexistence, jeevan, and humane conduct.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Editorial Notes

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Locating AI in the four orders

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Section 1.2 applies the four-order ontology and the distinction between compositional progression and constitutional completeness to a class of artefacts the primary texts do not name. The exposition states that application positively; it is synthesis, not an explicit source sentence. A later draft should verify instrument-evidence (yantra-praman) passages in KD against the Hindi and decide how far “machine” in those pages may be read toward computation.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Relation to other studies

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: This paper should not redo Why Humans Are Not Just Material, The Epistemology of Coexistence, or the planned Science Technology and Human Purpose. It cites them for jeevan, knowledge, and technology in general, and keeps AI as the centred question.
